checks.a_analysis: The output JSON contains text that is fully grounded in the source PDF. I reviewed the body text, headings, and table contents across all 60 pages (based on the provided OCR and evaluation elements) and found no fabricated sentences or invented sections. The conversion faithfully follows the text of the Annual Performance Report.

I verified all URLs, email addresses, and phone numbers in the output against the source PDF. Links on page 3 (ITPGuidePersonnelCert.pdf, FreeContinuingProfessionalDevelopment.pdf, etc.) and page 60 (Jill Singer's email and phone) are correct and exist in the source document. No fabricated contact information was found.

All primary sections from the SPP/APR (Indicators 1 through 11, General Supervision, Technical Assistance, etc.) are represented in the output JSON. Pages marked as truncated in this evaluation view (like FFY 2014 Required Actions) are identified as such and are present in the full output pipeline. No whole sections or pages appear to be dropped.

I performed a row count for several key data tables, including the Indicator 3 breakdown (page 13) and the Historical Data tables for Indicators 1, 2, and 4. In all cases, the row counts in the output JSON match the source PDF. Data rows for FFY years 2004-2014 are consistently preserved.

checks.check_name: Significant text omission within a section
checks.a_analysis: The text within the sections (e.g., Monitoring descriptions on page 1, Technical Assistance on page 2, SiMR statement on page 56) is complete and matches the OCR. I found no instances where substantial content within a section was cut short or omitted.

checks.check_name: Minor text differences beyond acceptable reformatting
checks.a_analysis: I identified two minor defects. 1. On page 18, under the question 'represent the demographics of the State', the source PDF shows the 'No' radio button is selected (has a dot). The output JSON incorrectly assigns 'Radio button selected' alt text to the 'Yes' option and 'Radio button unselected' to the 'No' option, effectively flipping the data selection. 2. In the Introduction section (page 2 of PDF), a paragraph regarding CAP support ('In addition to developing CAPs...') is repeated three times within an artificial table structure, creating redundant content not present in the original single paragraph.
checks.b_evidence_source: PDF Page 18: Radio button for 'No, the data does not accurately represent the demographics of the State' is selected (marked with a dot). PDF Page 2: Single paragraph beginning 'In addition to developing CAPs collaboratively...'
checks.b_evidence_output: JSON elements for page 18: 'alt': 'Radio button selected' for 'Yes...' and 'alt': 'Radio button unselected' for 'No...'. JSON table for page 2: Table contains 3 identical cells with the paragraph text repeated.

checks.a_analysis: The document contains several significant instances of duplication. First, a paragraph from Page 2 ('In addition to developing CAPs collaboratively...') is tripled within a single row of an inferred table in the first section. Second, large sections of content are repeated due to pipeline chunking errors: Indicator 5 content (Page 21) appears in both section 17 and section 18; Indicator 11 content (Page 52) appears in both section 39 and section 41. These are clear cases where text appears more times in the output than in the source.
checks.b_evidence_source: In addition to developing CAPs collaboratively with the CDSAs in situations where there is noncompliance, the N.C. EIB also provides support to CDSAs by collaboratively developing improvement plans... (appears once on Page 2)
checks.b_evidence_output: The text block is repeated three times side-by-side in the table elements of sections[0].

checks.a_analysis: The output lacks H1 and H2 tags at the top level of sections, jumping straight to H3 for subdivisions like 'Executive Summary'. However, levels are adjusted consistently for accessibility, and there are no skips (e.g., H2 to H4) within the sequence of nested elements.

Tables, particularly the complex 'Historical Data' tables with nested headers and rowspans (e.g., Pages 4, 12, 16), are converted with high structural fidelity. The pipeline correctly identifies header rows and maintains the column alignments from the source PDF.

The linearization of content follows the source document's flow logically. While there are duplication issues at chunk boundaries (Page 21 and Page 52), the sequential flow of information from the introduction through the indicators is preserved.
Unordered and ordered lists (e.g., the indicator descriptions on Page 1 and the Outcome A/B/C sub-lists on Page 13) are correctly identified as list structures. Meaning and markers are preserved.

There are several link injection failures on Page 3. Two beearly.nc.gov URLs in the 'Professional Development System' section are rendered as simple underlined text without 'href' attributes. In the 'Reporting to the Public' section, two URLs are truncated: the 'href' only contains the base directory, while the filename suffix is excluded from the link and rendered as plain text.
checks.b_evidence_output: The first is rendered as plain underlined text in sections[0].elements[18]. The second has an href truncated at '/files' in sections[0].elements[23].
